summary.text: Jim Baird is the Republican U.S. Representative for Indiana's 4th District and won re-election on November 3, 2026, according to unofficial results.

A Vietnam War veteran, farmer and Purdue-educated animal nutritionist, he served as a Putnam County commissioner and in the Indiana House before his 2018 election to Congress. He sits on the Agriculture, Science, Space, and Technology, and Foreign Affairs committees.

paragraphs.text: Baird was born in Fountain County, Indiana, in 1945, and his official biography describes him as a lifelong resident of West Central Indiana.

He earned bachelor's and master's degrees in animal science from Purdue University in 1967 and 1969, and, after returning from Vietnam, a doctorate in monogastric nutrition from the University of Kentucky in 1975.

He served in the U.S. Army from 1969 to 1972. His official biography describes him as a decorated Vietnam War veteran awarded a Bronze Star with V device and two Purple Hearts, and says his unit was inducted into the United States Transportation Corps Hall of Fame.
Before entering politics, Baird ran a home healthcare agency and a family farm and worked as a small business owner.

He served as Putnam County commissioner from 2006 to 2010, then in the Indiana House of Representatives from 2010 to 2018, including on the Ways and Means Committee, according to his official biography.

Baird was elected to the U.S. House in 2018. In the 119th Congress he serves on the Committee on Agriculture, where he is Vice Chair of the Conservation, Research, and Biotechnology subcommittee, and on the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology and the Committee on Foreign Affairs.
He won the May 5, 2026 Republican primary with 60.5% of the vote.
He won re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election with 54.2% of the vote to Drew Cox's 45.8%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.

According to his official biography, Baird is an active or former member of the Rotary Club of Greencastle, the Putnam County Fair and 4-H Club Association, VFW, American Legion and Indiana Farm Bureau, and served on the advisory council for Purdue University's Dean of Agriculture. He is married to Danise, and they have three children.
